evidence: Liv. 2.24: nē nōmina darent (Lewis & Short, s.v. nōmen)
terms.comment: Classically of enlisting for military service and of joining a group (dare nōmen in conjūrātiōnem); the plain way to say one signs up for something.
To declare oneself before an official: a candidate, a recruit, or each person at the census in Luke (ut profitērentur).

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 4: nōmen in tabulās (Lewis & Short, s.v. referō)
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase for signing the register at a hotel, built on Cicero’s in tabulās referre (see record).
To write someone’s name in a list: in cīvitātem ascrībere, to enrol as a citizen.

sources: Lewis & Short: nomen · Lewis & Short: profiteor · Lewis & Short: refero · Lewis & Short: ascribo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 370.
